devpost_page.title: LingoBuddy
devpost_page.tagline: LingoBuddy is an AI-powered language learning platform that makes mastering a new language engaging and personalized. LingoBuddy helps build confidence and fluency faster than ever.

sections.heading: Inspiration
sections.text: As language lovers, and very busy CS students with little to no free space for fun language classes, we are constantly disappointed about how hard it is to find language learning tools that are easy to use, quick, and speech/pronunciation focused. Duolingo is great (in spite of its recent, more-than-a-little creepy, animations), but lessons can feel tedious and the speech aspect is limited, especially for the free version.

sections.heading: What it does
sections.text: Thus, LingoBuddy was born! A Gemini AI-powered, customizable, language learning platform that balances the importance of language immersion with having a strong vocabulary to provide context for realistic conversations. LingoBuddy will generate custom lesson plans, exercises, and grammatical explanations based on chat input in either English or the target language. Additionally, Gemini will provide pronunciation help for users on vocabulary cards and sentence examples.

sections.heading: How we built it
sections.text: We used Next.js and bare-metal CSS for the frontend, Supabase for the database, and Python, FastAPI, and Gemini for the backend.

sections.heading: Challenges we ran into
sections.text: Gemini is great, however, the free plan is limited in its ability to accurately pronounce words and phrases from languages other than English. Ideally, we would have also implemented a 'live conversation' feature, where users could have dynamic conversations with Gemini. Due to time constraints, lack of knowledge about speech parsing, and difficulty with the latency of Gemini to generate responses, we were unable to accomplish these goals, but would like to in the future!

sections.heading: Accomplishments that we're proud of
sections.text: We are very proud of our UI - it's GORG. JK but not really. It did end up looking pretty nice, and we were able to overcome an unnecessary amount of difficulty implementing the typewriter animations, which was awesome. Additionally, as we are relatively new to project development, the custom login and AI integration features were very new to us, and we were able to get a (mostly) working product, which was also awesome.

sections.heading: What we learned
sections.text: We learned a LOT, most of which is listed below (anything that is missed is a result of too much screen time and lack of bloodflow due to too little movement): Authentication and data storage with Supabase Web development with Next.js Advanced CSS styling Gemini text-to-speech integration Gemini speech-to-text integration

sections.heading: What's next for LingoBuddy
sections.text: Our most immediate next steps for LingoBuddy are implementing the 'live conversation' features for our project. Additionally, we would like to make the language learning features quicker by storing past conversations or questions in our database or adjusting the voices of the generated speakers' voices to sound more natural and native to the language. We would also like to expand the profiles/dashboards for each user by tracking their progress in each language, storing vocabulary they've learned, common mistakes, etc. The future is bright for LingoBuddy, and we believe it has a lot of potential to keep multilingualism alive and well!

devpost_page.title: Sustainable Earth (Eco-Finance)
devpost_page.tagline: Imagine if every purchase you made could contribute to the fight against climate change. With our transaction tracking system, we provide people with an incentive to make purchases with intention.

sections.heading: Inspiration
sections.text: From climate change and extreme weather to environmental pollution to ecosystem degradation, we wanted to make a difference on the environment using finance. Taking inspiration from Acorn, an app which invests spare change, we wanted to invest small portions of money into eco-friendly companies for clients while also encouraging clients to spend green.

sections.heading: What it does
sections.text: Sustainable Earth is a banking application which tracks the client’s transactions, either through manually inputting a csv file or connecting with the client’s primary banking app with Plaid, and provides a eco-score for the user as well as other eco-friendly metrics. The user is then provided with recommended steps to take to decrease their carbon footprint and make more sustainable purchases. The user can then search for any product and the application will return the most sustainable option for the user to purchase as well as an eco-score for the product. The next part of the application is rewards. Based on a multiplier system, the user can purchase products based on their rewards credit through companies partnered with Sustainable Earth. In addition, users can invest their rewards money in eco-friendly companies. In the investments page, the user is asked to answer questions for the application to obtain a grasp on the user’s financial situation and risk preference.

sections.heading: How we built it
sections.text: We first thought of an idea that we all liked. Then we shared a repository and began coding. We used multiple technologies to make our functionalities work. We then created the front end using latest tech like tailwind and react. Then we created and tested the backend code and our prompts for the LLM APIs. After, we connected the frontend and backend using tech like flask and express. Finally we had our friends attempt to break the “product” and fix as many bugs as possible!

sections.heading: Challenges we ran into
sections.text: Figuring out how to obtain user transaction data was difficult, so we ended up using Plaid. We also had trouble with developing an effective visualization for the user’s active investments, ended up implementing yfinance api to fetch live stock data. Had trouble parsing web-scraped data specifically for application usage, fixed by using Gemini API which did parsing for us instead.

sections.heading: Accomplishments that we're proud of
sections.text: We're proud of being able to integrate Gemini into our search engine for environmentally product options and green stocks, allowing users to help the environment through everyday tasks like shopping and investing. We are also proud of our UI and the use of Plaid API to retrieve user banking data. Finally, we are proud of our team bonding exercises and our accountability in finishing each part of the project on time.

sections.heading: What we learned
sections.text: Learned how to use Gemini API for multiple aspects of our project. Learned how to connect Plaid API with application using Plaid’s mock account.

sections.heading: What's next for Sustainable Earth (Eco-Finance)
sections.text: The next step that we plan to take is to work with banks to sponsor real-money cashback rewards for customers who have environmentally friendly spending habits. We also plan to gamify this experience through achievements, streaks, and a leaderboard encouraging player competition. Combined, these additions will increase player engagement and make a larger impact towards the environment.

devpost_page.title: Helix
devpost_page.tagline: Pick a cancer type and protein target. Helix screens thousands of compounds and ranks the top candidates with real quantum circuits, allowing researchers to identify highly targeted candidates.

sections.heading: How we built it
sections.text: We built Helix in three layers. The first layer pulls 14,000 real drug compounds from ChEMBL, the world's largest open drug database, and trains a machine learning model on real lab experiments for each cancer protein target. The second layer runs every compound through that model to narrow 14,000 options down to 10 candidates in seconds. The third layer runs a real quantum algorithm called VQE on each of those 10 drugs to compute how stable the molecule is at a quantum chemistry level, giving researchers an extra signal that no standard tool produces.

sections.heading: Challenges we ran into
sections.text: Getting quantum circuits to work on real drug molecules was harder than expected because quantum chemistry requires molecules to have an even number of electrons, and most drug fragments do not. We had to write custom preprocessing logic to fix each molecule before it would run without crashing. Cleaning the training data was also a big challenge since the raw database had duplicate experiments and inconsistent measurements that we had to filter out before the models could learn anything useful.

sections.heading: Accomplishments that we are proud of
sections.text: Every number in Helix comes from a real source. The machine learning models were trained on thousands of real lab experiments, the quantum energies are real circuit outputs, and the drug library is real ChEMBL data. We are also proud that the system never just breaks. If a model is missing, it falls back to similarity screening automatically, and if the backend is off, the frontend still works on cached data.

sections.heading: What we learned
sections.text: Quantum computing is a very specific tool and knowing where it fits matters more than using it everywhere. We also learned that the real problem in drug discovery is not speed, it is that 96% of drugs fail in clinical trials because early screening misses too many good candidates.

sections.heading: What is next for Helix
sections.text: We want to scale the quantum layer to run on real IBM quantum hardware, which we already have the integration built for and just need hardware access to turn on. On the machine learning side, we want to switch to graph neural networks that reason about the shape of a molecule instead of a flat fingerprint, which should make predictions significantly more accurate. Long term, we want the system to learn from real lab results so every experiment a researcher runs makes the next round of predictions better.

devpost_page.title: Data Engineer's Buddy
devpost_page.tagline: Using ArangoDB & NetworkX for AI-powered management of enterprise data

sections.heading: Inspiration
sections.text: Problem Statement Data in large organizations is spread across multiple DBs on several different DBMS This results in a significant cost of operation from a data engineering standpoint. Proposal Over the course of this hackathon, I've explored how ArangoDB & NetworkX can be used to aid AI in the management of enterprise data. A variety of tasks such as data cataloging, lineage tracking, day-to-day data operations which traditionally requires the collaboration of several teams could be done within minutes by storing the metadata in a multimodal DB such as ArangoDB. Packages & libraries such as NetworkX & CuGraph can then be leveraged by AI agents to deliver insights & perform data engineering tasks within minutes. The multimodal offering of ArangoDB allows for metadata to be stored in such a way that a variety of data engineering tasks can easily be performed withing minutes.

sections.heading: What it does
sections.text: Note: For this hackathon, I've focused on the data engineering tasks that can be performed by AI agents as that is universal & applicable to all enterprises. DEBy - Data Engineer's Buddy is an intelligent agentic app that assists with Data Operations in Enterprises At this stage, DEBy is able to: Identify upstreams & downstreams Assist with ETL Refresh scheduling Intelligently calculate refresh delays Perform impact analysis resulting from changes in a data model

sections.heading: How we built it
sections.text: Data - I've stored the relationships between data structures in the form of Arango Graph & metadata such as refresh details in the form of Arango Collections App - Created using Python, LangChain, LangGraph & OpenAI API

sections.heading: Challenges we ran into
sections.text: Identifying the best way to leverage multimodal features of ArangoDB to capture the structure of enterprise data Agent had to learn the relationships between enterprise data structures & the nature of dependencies Teaching the agent data operation tasks

sections.heading: Accomplishments that we're proud of
sections.text: Using ArangoDB to capture the relationships between SQL objects & storing metadata critical for Data Operations Agent can identify upstream & downstream dependencies & intuitively understand the implications of dependencies with minimal prompting. Agent can perform easily perform tedious Data Operation tasks such as refresh scheduling & lineage tracking The agent can create visualizations for all of the above features

sections.heading: What we learned
sections.text: ArangoDB's multimodal features can be easily used to capture information about enterprise data structures. Using NetworkX & CuGraph, the data can be parsed in realtime by AI agents to extract insights & automate complex Data Operations tasks.

sections.heading: What's next for DEBy
sections.text: Create an enterprise ready solution leveraging ArangoDB to simplify management of enterprise data Additional features for DEBy that aims to automate complex Data Operation tasks Leverage the multimodal features of ArangoDB to make DEBy the one-stop solution for all of enterprise specific requirements of a Data Engineer

devpost_page.title: Dice Aid
devpost_page.tagline: DiceAid is an automatic dice roller designed with unbiased rolling and precise score calculation mechanics. Its goal is to help game players who face challenges with traditional dice mechanics.

sections.heading: Inspiration
sections.text: A few of our members are in a course called ECE 202, where one of our professors gave us an exam that studied the different Yahtzee scoring patterns in excel. This sparked our creativity initially lead us down the automated dice rolling path. We started with the idea of an automatic Yahtzee roller, but how useful is that? We then thought of D&D, but that still felt very narrow. With time, we realized that an automatic dice roller could be work across any game, and support participants of all abilities. By the end, we decided DiceAid's mission would be to offer accessible unbiased rolling for anyone who may struggle with traditional dice rolling mechanics.

sections.heading: What it does
sections.text: The DiceAid takes a set of dice, and with the press of a button, launches them into the play area where they are then analyzed and the swept up again. On the attached screen, an image of the dice will be displayed as well as their sum total.

sections.heading: How we built it
sections.text: Our team is comprised of diverse engineering talent that made Dice Aid possible: Our amazing MechE, David did some outstanding CAD work and designed the 3-D the shell of our system Our EE, Artem devloped the interface between our Raspberry Pi 4B and stepper motors. Our CompE, Felicite built the UI and dice recognition for the program. Throughout the project, we collaborated closely and helped each other tremendously along the way.

sections.heading: Challenges we ran into
sections.text: Our biggest challenge was getting a camera connected to our Raspberry Pi, in fact we went through 5 cameras, and we even drove to Target and bought a new one to no avail. In the end we finally found a working Raspberry Pi compatible camera and got to work. Our second largest challenge would most likely be in the fine tuning of our stepper motors in order for them to correctly roll the dice, it took a while and required minor adjustments in both their wiring and their programing.

sections.heading: Accomplishments that we're proud of
sections.text: The moment that we had a working camera that could take photos and show them onto our UI we were ecstatic. That was probably the most rewarding portion of our work. Later, our next big milestone got us excited, when we got the dot recognition to work! It signified that we were on our way to the finish line.

sections.heading: What we learned
sections.text: Felicite had never programmed a Raspberry Pi before nor had any experience with stepper motors, this was also her first hackathon and it taught her more than most of her class have. David learned how to efficiently program stepper motors and improved his CAD design, it was also his first hackathon! Artem learned how to code on a Raspberry Pi along with how to work the interface between stepper motors and their code, this was his second hackathon, but his first submitting a project!

sections.heading: What's next for Dice Aid
sections.text: Our next step is to explore DiceAid's artistic potential. We envision dice environments that reflect the game, like D&D. We'd hope that with more artistic flare, the DiceAid would feel less robotic and clinical, combining functionality and ambiance perfectly fitting for a gaming experience.

devpost_page.title: DoubleTake
devpost_page.tagline: You never have to go alone to a date again! Double Take allows you to partner up with your friend and find a match in a group setting in hopes of forming friendships or potentially something more!

sections.heading: Inspiration
sections.text: Our inspiration came straight from the room here at SFU! A teammate in our tram is single, and when a dating event was announced here at the hackathon, our teammate felt super nervous and anxious about the thought of going alone. As we were hyping them up, we joked about how much easier and less terrifying it would be if we could all just go together as a squad to brave the singles scene or better yet, find someone as a team. That sparked the whole idea: why not build a platform that matches people based on shared "vibes" and duos, making dating and meeting new people fun, social, and way less intimidating?

sections.heading: What it does
sections.text: DoubleTake is a dating platform that allows you to partner up with your best friend and find a match with another pair. It solves the interview-like process of regular dating apps which focuses more on individual prospects and commonly used (dry) pickup lines. It's safer, less pressure, and a lot more fun, because your best friend comes too. Key Features include : Duo - Create a single profile for you and your friend, finding a shared interest and making Discovery Feed - Find and match your next double date through a single swipe. Search - Search based on common filter types and hobbies another pair may have as well as potential vibes based on TiDB's Algorithm . Matchs - Every duo you like matches you back and you enter the messaging groupchat Your Duo - Your Duo profile with your friend

sections.heading: How we built it
sections.text: Frontend (Jill) : Jill used react for the pages which uses hooks to load the data of the user and to know who the current user is. She created an api.js that either asks the fake back end in mocks or sends the real request through the httpClient.js into a Spring boot API. Components were used as reusable blocks that pages were assembled from and the context folder is shared the the current duo and user on every screen. Jill used tailwind for the CSS with the assistance of Claude Code to ideate and sort out technical bugs and structural plans of the project. Database/Backend (Valerie) : Valerie built some of the backend infrastructure using Java Spring Boot, connecting it directly to a cloud TiDB database to manage our application data and user profiles. She engineered the backend architecture, handled the database persistence layer, and integrated the vector search features so the app could process and match data smoothly. Backend (Annie) : I built part of the backend infrastructure and database architecture using Java Spring Boot and TiDB. I developed the main application logic, engineering the REST controllers and service layers to handle user workflows, while designing, adding, and structuring the database tables to securely persist our application data.

sections.heading: Challenges we ran into
sections.text: Frontend (Jill): Tailwind's long class lists were frustrating, but Jill saw its value for building quickly without separate CSS files. Her biggest challenge was building a mock API that matched exactly what the real backend would return, including data shapes and error codes. She solved it by working backwards from each screen to identify the functions needed, creating one mock function per endpoint from the team's API contract, and adding a single setting to switch between mock and real data. Database/Backend (Valerie) : Integrating the vector search functionality was a major hurdle, setting up the AI embedding pipeline to translate plain-English descriptions into accurate vector queries for TiDB required careful handling. We also had to troubleshoot cloud deployment networking, resolving CORS blocking between our local frontend and our Render backend. Backend (Annie) : One of our biggest hurdles was successfully bridging the gap between our frontend and backend. Connecting the client-side interface to the live API endpoints required troubleshooting network routing, handling data mapping discrepancies, and ironing out communication bugs so the frontend could seamlessly send and receive data from the server.

sections.heading: Accomplishments that we're proud of
sections.text: Frontend (Jill): Bringing the entire user experience to life by building a sleek, responsive interface that seamlessly translates complex user interactions and smooth navigation into an intuitive, polished client-side app. Database\Backend (Valerie): Architecting the backend services and integrating the cutting-edge AI vector-embedding pipeline (⁠AiEmbeddingService.java⁠) that allows our app to perform intelligent, plain-text semantic "vibe matching" directly inside our cloud database. Database\ Backend (Annie): Engineering the core backend infrastructure, building out robust REST controllers, managing the service layer logic, and structuring and adding the relational database tables to ensure rock-solid data flow and persistence.

sections.heading: What we learned
sections.text: Frontend (Jill) : Jill earned how React projects are structured, from reusable components and routing to sharing state with context, and how Tailwind integrates through Vite. Jill practiced hooks, promises and API calls, and adopted better JavaScript practices like centralizing API calls, handling loading and error states, and documenting functions. Database/Backend (Valerie) : Valerie learned that when we set our minds to a goal, we can pick up entirely new technologies and build complex full-stack features in a remarkably short amount of time. Even though I had no prior experience with a lot of this tech stack before starting, this project showed me how fast we can learn, prototype, and ship a fully functional, AI-powered application from scratch. Backend (Annie) : I learned how rapidly we can design, build, and deploy a robust backend system from scratch when diving into new technologies. This project taught me the ins and outs of structuring scalable Java architectures, managing database schemas, and successfully integrating client-server communication under a tight timeframe.

sections.text: PiggyBank: Make your money talk!

sections.heading: 💡 Inspiration: The Invisible Spending Problem
sections.text: We built PiggyBank because personal finance has quietly become one of the biggest sources of everyday stress. Most people don’t struggle because of big, one-time purchases. They struggle because of the tiny, invisible habits — a $6 coffee here, a $12 delivery there — that quietly drain financial confidence and compound stress over time. The Financial Anxiety Data 65% of Americans live paycheck to paycheck. (LendingClub, 2024) 77% of adults feel anxious about money. (APA, 2023) 59% of Gen Z and Millennials admit to impulse purchases. (Credit Karma)

sections.heading: 🎯 Use Case: Awareness in the Moment
sections.text: We built Piggy to do more than just track spending — it’s an agent quietly working in the background, learning your financial habits and helping you make smarter choices. Imagine this: you tap your card at Starbucks, and Piggy takes note. Over time, it learns that you grab coffee every day around 8 a.m. Since Piggy is designed to understand your behavioral patterns, it predicts when your next purchase is coming — and before you buy(say at 7.30), it sends a friendly iMessage nudge: “Hey, maybe try a cheaper alternative like Wawa today? You ould be a day closer to your new bike that you are saving for.” You reply, and Piggy keeps learning. Soon, it’s not just tracking your spending — it’s helping you visualize how small choices add up. Instead of cutting out your morning coffee entirely, Piggy helps you see how redirecting those savings could make your new $250 bike a reality faster than you thought. Piggy doesn’t guilt-trip you — it guides you, helping you reflect at the moment when awareness matters most. Also, to reduce user friction, if you do an in-person purchase AKA have receipts, just text them to piggy, and he'll handle the rest! Super Simple!

sections.heading: ✨ What It Does: A Real-Time Financial Conscience
sections.text: PiggyBank is a real-time spending coach powered by a feedback loop that connects your transactions to a conversational agent. Core Functionality Item-Level Transaction Ingestion: Uses the Knot ** Production **TransactionLink API to ingest granular, item-level purchase data into Snowflake securely. Real-Time Classification & Feedback: Each purchase triggers a real-time loop: The backend uses Dedalus to classify the item (Need/Want). Sends a personalized message via Photon to your iMessage for quick feedback. Your reply fine-tunes Piggy’s predictions. Proactive Prediction: Detects recurring spends and sends nudges before they happen. Multimodal Receipt Processing: Powered by Gemini 2.5 Flash — users can snap a photo of a receipt, and Piggy instantly extracts structured data via OCR. “Oink oink! I’ve analyzed your receipt from Courtyard by Marriott. Total: $23.67. Saved to your tracker!” Contextual Chat Assistant: A GPT-4–powered chat assistant that reads live Snowflake history to answer: “How much did I spend on coffee this month?” or “What could I cut to save $50 next week?”

sections.heading: 🧠 How Our Algorithm is Made (Deployed on DigitalOcean)
sections.text: Our predictive and conversational intelligence layer runs on a modular, serverless architecture using DigitalOcean Gradient AI . 1. Data Foundation & Feature Store (Snowflake) All transaction data and user feedback are stored in Snowflake, serving as the feature store where SQL queries and vector search aggregate behavioral patterns. 2. Predictive Behavior Model (DigitalOcean Gradient AI) Llama 3.1 is deployed to intelligently ingest these datapoints and predict when the next purchase is likely to occur, allowing the agent to proactively trigger timely recommendations. With the help of Python data processing and Snowflake time-series model analyzes each user’s purchase history, computes typical intervals between repeat buys, and produces a numeric next-purchase timestamp plus confidence. Piggy analyzes factors such as the size of previous orders (e.g., whether a grocery trip typically covers a week or a month) and historical spending frequency to forecast upcoming transactions with high accuracy. 3. Classification & Logic (Dedalus Labs) Dedalus handles initial transaction classification and confidence scoring before engaging users via Photon. 4. Multimodal Processing (Gemini API) Receipt image processing via Gemini 2.5 Flash enables OCR and JSON extraction before saving structured data to Snowflake.

sections.text: Layer Technologies Key Use Backend / API FastAPI (Python), Flask, Node.js Microservices, RESTful endpoints, Core Analytics Data Warehouse Snowflake Central time-series storage and analytics Integrations Knot API, Clerk Auth Secure item-level data ingestion, Auth Conversational AI Photon, iMessage SDK Real-time chat, proactive alerts Intelligence Gemini 2.5 Flash, Dedalus, GPT4, Llama 3.1, DO Gradient AI OCR, Classification, Prediction Frontend React (Vite), Clerk Auth Dashboard and visualization

devpost_page.tagline: MediGuide is an AI-powered system that ensures medication adherence through personalized reminders via automated phone calls, improving patient safety and reducing health risks.

sections.heading: Inspiration 🎯
sections.text: Medication non-persistence is a critical issue affecting patient safety in the United States and beyond. According to studies, "between 40% and 75% of adults fail to take their prescribed medications on time each day" [1], leading to worsening health outcomes, increased hospitalizations, and preventable deaths. Non-adherence can lead to serious complications, including "delirium, hypoglycemia, and acute kidney injury" [2]. Existing digital reminder solutions often suffer from high onboarding friction, making them less accessible to those who need them most—particularly senior citizens and less privileged members of society who may have limited access to or knowledge of modern technology like smartphones or the internet. We were inspired to create MediGuide to address these gaps, providing an inclusive, user-friendly solution that enhances medication adherence and improves patient safety for everyone.

sections.heading: What It Does 💊
sections.text: MediGuide is an AI-powered reminder and monitoring system designed to enhance patient safety by ensuring adherence to medication regimens. Here's how it works: 1️⃣ Seamless Onboarding with Healthcare Professionals: Patients are onboarded through a consultation session with a healthcare professional, either in-person or via telehealth. The doctor understands the patient's needs, writes a prescription, and enters it into the MediGuide platform, specifying the patient's preferred method of reminder. 2️⃣ Personalized Reminder Delivery: MediGuide's intelligent AI system identifies the medication and dosage, setting up personalized reminders for the patient via their chosen method—automated phone calls or text messages. Each reminder includes clear, simple instructions tailored to the patient's specific medication regimen. 3️⃣ Monitoring and Feedback: After each reminder, the system prompts the patient to confirm medication intake. It periodically checks in about their experiences, detecting early signs of adverse reactions and prompting timely interventions. 4️⃣ AI-Powered Adaptation: The AI continuously learns from patient behavior, using predictive analytics to adapt and optimize reminders for each individual, improving adherence over time. By integrating this data-driven approach, MediGuide aims to minimize medication-related risks, reduce hospital readmissions, and ultimately improve overall patient safety.

sections.heading: How We Built It 🛠️
sections.text: We built MediGuide using Next.js and Flask for the backend, providing a robust and scalable infrastructure. The frontend was developed with React.js, TypeScript, and shadcn, ensuring a responsive and user-friendly interface. To understand doctors' prescriptions and generate smart, personalized reminders, we utilized top-performing Large Language Models (LLMs). For the phone call reminders, we leveraged advanced conversational voice AI technologies to deliver engaging and accessible interactions with patients who may not be familiar with modern digital devices.

sections.heading: Challenges We Ran Into 🚧
sections.text: One of the main challenges we faced was integrating advanced AI technologies within a tight time frame. Developing an AI system that accurately understands and processes doctors' prescriptions required careful tuning of Large Language Models. Ensuring that our platform is accessible to patients with limited technological proficiency was another challenge, as we needed to design interfaces and interaction methods (like phone calls) that are user-friendly for all age groups and technological backgrounds. Additionally, we had to consider compliance with healthcare regulations and patient privacy laws, which added complexity to our development process.

sections.heading: Accomplishments That We're Proud Of 🎉
sections.text: We are proud of being able to create MediGuide in under 36 hours for a noble cause. Developing a functional AI-powered system capable of understanding prescriptions, generating personalized reminders, and interacting with patients through conversational voice AI within such a short time frame was a significant achievement. We hope that this creation can eventually evolve into a product that helps more patients take their medications timely and recover faster, improving patient safety for millions across the world.

sections.heading: What We Learned 📚
sections.text: Throughout this project, we learned about the complexities surrounding medication adherence and the significant impact it has on patient safety and healthcare costs. We gained valuable experience in integrating advanced AI technologies, such as Large Language Models and conversational voice AI, into a practical application. Additionally, we learned the importance of designing solutions that are accessible and user-friendly for all patients, regardless of their technological proficiency. This project reinforced the value of interdisciplinary collaboration between technology and healthcare to address real-world problems.

sections.heading: What's Next for MediGuide 🚀
sections.text: We're excited to hear feedback from our peers and mentors and to speak with actual healthcare practitioners. Our next steps involve engaging with medical professionals to gather insights and validate our solution in real-world settings. We aim to explore avenues of collaboration with hospitals and clinics to integrate MediGuide into existing healthcare systems, ultimately improving patient safety on a larger scale. We're also considering further development to comply with healthcare regulations, enhance AI capabilities, and expand accessibility features to reach more patients. Citations

devpost_page.title: FireWatch
devpost_page.tagline: 🔥 FireWatch: AI-Driven Wildfire Response & Prediction for Quebec 🔥

sections.text: FireWatch: AI-Powered Wildfire Response & Prediction

sections.heading: 🔥 Inspiration
sections.text: Wildfires have become an increasingly critical issue in Quebec, with devastating impacts on communities, wildlife, and infrastructure. We wanted to create a smart, data-driven solution that optimizes firefighting resource allocation and predicts future fire occurrences, helping emergency services act faster, smarter, and more efficiently .

sections.heading: 🛠 How We Built It
sections.text: We developed FireWatch using a combination of data processing, optimization algorithms, and machine learning to tackle both wildfire response and prediction. Part 1: Resource Deployment Optimization Processed real-time wildfire reports from current_wildfiredata.csv . Implemented an optimized allocation system that prioritizes high-severity fires while considering deployment time and resource constraints. Calculated both operational costs and damage costs from missed responses. Generated a comprehensive report summarizing firefighting efficiency. Part 2: Predictive Modeling for Future Fire Occurrences (Optional, but powerful!) Analyzed historical fire and environmental data from 2020-2023 . Used machine learning models (skLearn) to predict fire-prone areas for 2025 . Integrated Mapbox to visualize predicted fire locations on a map of Quebec.

sections.heading: 🚀 Challenges We Faced
sections.text: Balancing resource allocation: Ensuring fair deployment while minimizing missed responses. Optimizing response time: Factoring in different firefighting unit speeds and availability. Data inconsistencies: Cleaning and handling missing values in historical data. Map visualization: Integrating a clear, interactive wildfire risk map for future fire predictions.

sections.heading: 🎯 What We Learned
sections.text: The importance of real-time decision-making in emergency scenarios. How to apply optimization algorithms to resource allocation problems. Leveraging machine learning for environmental hazard prediction. Using Mapbox and geospatial tools to visualize fire risks effectively.

sections.heading: 🔥 Impact
sections.text: FireWatch can help emergency teams reduce response times, lower wildfire damage costs, and improve disaster preparedness , making Quebec safer for everyone.
